questions.question: If P is 200% of Q and R is 400% of Q, then R is how much percent more than P?
questions.solution:
Given,

P is 200% of Q and R is 400% of Q

P = 200/ 100 × Q

P = 2Q

R = 400 / 100 × Q

R = 4Q

R is more than P by = 4Q - 2Q / 2Q × 100

= 2Q / 2Q × 100

= 100

R is 100 % more than P.

Hence, “100” is the correct answer.

questions.question: Ratio of the present ages of Mohan and Ram is 3 : 5 and the difference between their ages is 12 years. What is the present age (in years) of Ram?
questions.solution:
Let the present ages of Mohan and Ram be 3x and 5x

Difference between their ages = 12

5x – 3x = 12

2x = 12

x = 6

Ram’s present age = 5x = 5 × 6 = 30

Hence, “30’ is the correct answer.

questions.question: Which Article of Indian Constitution gives definition of money bill?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option **2** i.e __**Article 110.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 110** of the Indian Constitution gives the definition of a money bill.

 
 
• A money bill is a bill that deals with the imposition, emission, abolition, alteration, or regulation of any tax, regulating the borrowing power of the state.
 
• **Loksabha** has the exclusive authority over a money bill.
 
• Money bills of the union can be introduced **only in Lok Sabha.**
 
• A money bill must be returned to the Lok Sabha within** 14 days** if there is any recommended amendment by the Rajya Sabha.
 
• **The speaker of the Lok sabha** has a special power to certify a money bill.
 
• President **can not return the money bill **for the reconsideration of the parliament.
 
• A money bill can be introduced in parliament only with the prior permission of the President of India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 56** of the Indian Constitution deals with the term of office of the Indian President.
 
• **Article 72** of the Indian Constitution deals with the pardoning power of the President.
 
• **Article 121** of the Indian Constitution deals with the Restriction on discussion in Parliament.

questions.question:
Under which condition/conditions a member of parliament can be disqualified?

I. If he holds office of profit under Government of India

II. If disqualified by any law.

III. If he is an undischarged in solvent
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option **4** i.e __**All I, II, and III.**__

 
• A member who elected by the people of a particular constituency and represents those people in the parliament is called a **Member of Parliament (MP).**
 
• A Member of Parliament can be from any of the two houses of the Indian Parliament namely Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha.
 
• Parliament is constituted under **Article 79** of the Indian constitution.
 
• The parliament consists of **Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, and the President of India.**
 
• **Rajya Sabha** is constituted under **Article 80** of the Indian constitution.
 
 
• The Rajya Sabha is also called the **house of elders.**
 
• The maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha is fixed to **250 members.**
 
• Among the 250 members, 238 members represent the States and Union Territories, and 12 members are nominated by the President.
 
• Rajya Sabha is a **permanent body** not subjected to dissolution.
 
 
 
• **Lok Sabha** is constituted under **Article 81** of the Indian constitution.
 
 
• The Lok Sabha is also called the House of the People.
 
• The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha is fixed to** 552 members.**
 
• Among the 552 members, 530 members represent the States, 20 members represent Union Territories, and 2 members are nominated by the President.
 
• At present, there are **545 members** in Lok Sabha.
 
 
 
• **A member of parliament can be disqualified under the following conditions**
 
 
• **If he holds the office of profit under the Government of India**
 
• **If disqualified by any law.**
 
• **If he is an undischarged insolvent.**
 
• **If he has ceased to be a citizen of India.**
 
• **If he disqualified on the ground of defection.**

• Muhammad bin Tughluq was the Sultan of Delhi.
 
 
• He is also known as the **wisest fool.**
 
• He ruled the Tughlaq dynasty from **1325 to 1351.**
 
• He moved his capital from **Delhi to ****Daulatabad** in 1327.
 
• After two years he shifted the capital back to Delhi due to lack of water supplies and many other issues.
 
• He introduced** **the** 'token' currency** in 1330.
 
• The coins introduced by Muhammad bin Tughlaq were made of **brass and copper.**
 
• The values of the coins were equal to that of gold and silver coins.
 
• The use of token currency has stopped in 1333 due to the issues in trade and commerce.

questions.question: In which city, the Jalianwala Bagh massacre happened?

• It happened in **Amritsar,** Punjab.
 
• The protest against the **Rowlatt Act** led to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
 
• British officer General **Reginald Dyer** ordered troops of the British Indian Army to fire into a crowd of unarmed Indian civilians.
 
• The governor of Punjab during the massacre was **Michael O' Dyer.**
 
• **Udham Singh** killed **Michael O' Dyer **as a revenge for the massacre.
 
• The Jallianwala Bagh massacre happened during the Indian festival **Baisakhi.**
 
• The Hunter Commission was appointed by the British government to study the massacre.
 
• Rabindranath Tagore renounced his knighthood as a protest against the massacre.
 
 
 
• Britain expressed "regret" on the Jallianwala Bagh incident in 2019.
